newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN attacks Portugal over East Timor.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN attacks Portugal over East Timor.

text.p: The seven members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations attacked Portugal over East Timor on Saturday and accused Lisbon of aggravating relations between ASEAN and the European Union.

"The ASEAN heads of government noted with increasing concern the efforts of one member country of the EU to introduce extraneous issues such as the question of East Timor in the economic cooperation and interaction between ASEAN and the EU," ASEAN leaders said after a one-day summit.
In a post-summit news conference, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas named Portugal and said Lisbon was "making the East Timor issue a condition for ASEAN-EU cooperation".
Indonesian troops invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975, and the territory was named Indonesia's 27th province the following July.
The United Nations has refused to recognise Indonesian sovereignty over East Timor and still regards Portugal as the administering power.
The ASEAN leaders' statement said "they believed that the introduction of such an extraneous issue (as East Timor) would only lead to unwarranted aggravation in ASEAN-EU relations".
"They (Lisbon) have failed to achieve their purpose so far but it has become increasingly an irritant in the relationship between ASEAN and the EU," it said.
Alatas said Indonesia had raised the issue at the summit and "got full support from all the other heads of government of ASEAN".
ASEAN groups Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam and Brunei.
